messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — latency_regression detected for redwood-runtime: p95 > 500ms for 3m across us-west-1, paging on-call. link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/2392001234
pagerduty: Paging on-call: @Cheng (primary), @Samir (backup) — incident created 2392001234
Cheng: on it, joining. initial symptoms?
Samir: saw a spike on the p95 -> ~800ms across several routes. p50 barely moved (35ms -> 45ms) but p95 jumped.
Devon: confirmed in dashboards — model gen routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat. per-route p95: generate 780ms, chat 820ms. throughput steady.
Evelyn: taking traffic analysis — no config deploys in last 2h per deploy-bot. Looking up infra changes.
Priya: I see host-level kernel upgrades were rolled out to a partial pool in us-west-1 ~ 38m ago (kmod: kernel-6.6.0-rollback?). pulling change events.
Cheng: good lead. can someone collect representative traces for a slow and a normal request? attach spans and logs here.
Samir: attaching two spans (slow vs normal). pasted snippets below:
```
Slow request spans:
- request.start
- routing.kv_cache.lookup 120ms
- model.attention.forward 310ms
- gpu_enqueue.wait 90ms
- network.serialize 50ms
- request.end
Total ~ 780ms
```
```
Normal request spans:
- request.start
- routing.kv_cache.lookup 10ms
- model.attention.forward 20ms
- gpu_enqueue.wait 15ms
- request.end
Total ~ 45ms
```
Devon: KV cache lookup is huge in slow case. That suggests something is stalling host-side IO or scheduler preemption.
Evelyn: grabbing host perf counters from affected instance i-0a12b3c4d:
```
# sar -q 1 3
00:00:01 runq-sz  plist-sz  ldavg-1
...  27  110  6.40
```
```
# vmstat 1 3
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ----cpu----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si so bi  bo  in  cs us sy id wa st
 9  0      0  220M  12M   1.1G   0  0  35  18  400 1200 60 20  5 15 0
```
Priya: noticed high runnable queue (r ~9) on those hosts after the kernel rollout.
Cheng: timeline so far: 00:38 kernel rollout started to subset of us-west pool -> 00:55 p95 begins rising -> 01:05 alert fires -> 01:10 page.
Samir: hypothesis 1: kernel change modified scheduler preemption or changed IRQ affinity handling causing long-runnable bursts that block host threads handling KV cache (rocksdb) IO.
Devon: hypothesis 2: a NIC driver change with kernel brought different rx/tx behavior — causing longer serialization on enqueue paths.
Evelyn: to test: can we temporarily drift traffic off the upgraded hosts? If p95 drops, it's infra.
Cheng: @infra — can we tag and cordon one AZ pool subset and shift requests away? fallback policy: route to older kernel node pool.
Priya: started cordon/evict on 6 hosts (targeted). will update when traffic cutover complete.
Samir: also requesting application-level mitigation: enable KV cache bypass (force model to fetch from faster in-memory replication) — config flag: runtime.kv_cache.strict=false — will reduce consistency but cut lookup stalls. Any objections?
Devon: ok to enable for canary subset (5% of traffic) while we observe. Evelyn pls watch error rates.
Evelyn: canary enabled at 01:20 for 5% traffic. p95 on canary dropped to 60ms within 30s. main pool still high.
Cheng: strong signal: infra change is causal. keep canary and continue draining/upgrading. Priya please escalate kernel change with platform team and include exact builds.
Priya: kernel builds: older nodes running kernel-6.5.12; upgraded nodes running kernel-6.6.0-rc2+backports (rpm: kernel-6.6.0-rc2-2026.1). rolling started at 00:38 by autoscaler. filing ops-ticket: #OPS-4121.
Samir: collecting perf data - asking for perf script capture on one upgraded and one non-upgraded host. run:
```
sudo perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 60
sudo perf script -i /tmp/perf.data > /tmp/perf.txt
```
and paste /tmp/perf.txt here.
Devon: also run eBPF trace for kv cache syscall latencies: rdk-trace kv_lookup -o /tmp/kv.json --duration 60s
Cheng: customer-impact note: approx 18% of requests in us-west saw p95 > 500ms during peak window. Top impacted customers: Acme Corp (4% of global TPS), DataBuddy (2.7%), several smaller PLG apps. No data loss reported.
Priya: mitigation status: cordon + canary KV bypass -> overall p95 for region dropped from 820ms -> 95ms by 01:30. continuing to cordon remaining upgraded hosts and draining.
Evelyn: metrics post-mitigation: CPU runqueue back to normal, sar runq-sz -> 2, vmstat r -> 1, latency p95 stable ~90ms.
Samir: perf differences: on upgraded host perf script shows heavy stack in softirq and __do_softirq, and traces show long delays in futex/wake paths for worker threads. Non-upgraded host shows normal distribution in model.attention.
Devon: this aligns with NIC/IRQ/coalescing changes or scheduler tick behavior change in kernel-6.6.0.
Cheng: next steps (in-thread):
- Priya: escalate kernel rollback plan with platform + change control, include perf traces and timeline. (assigned)
- Samir: collate traces and attach full perf.txt and eBPF dumps. (assigned)
- Devon: prepare rollback playbook to shift traffic back to older kernel nodes if rollback approved. (assigned)
- Evelyn: customer comms draft with impact summary and mitigation steps. (assigned)
- Cheng: prepare RCA doc skeleton once we have perf + kernel vendor analysis. (assigned)
Priya: created vendor ticket to kernel team: KERN-5678. noted potential regression in softirq handling and NAPI polling behavior.
Samir: attaching perf excerpt:
```
# perf top excerpt (upgraded)
  25.4%  [kernel] __do_softirq
  18.1%  [kernel] napi_poll
  12.2%  [libc] futex_wait
  9.3%   redwood::kv::lookup
```
```
# perf top excerpt (non-upgraded)
  6.2%   [kernel] __do_softirq
  4.1%   [kernel] napi_poll
  2.3%   redwood::kv::lookup
```
Devon: nice diffs. We should consider temporary NIC interrupt affinity tuning as a short-term mitigation on upgraded hosts if rollback is delayed. Command to try (one-off):
```
echo 1 > /proc/irq/<irq>/smp_affinity
```
Cheng: but we prefer routing off the pool while we do a safe rollback. platform ETA for a decision?
Priya: vendor response expected in 2-3 hours; platform prefers rollback to last stable kernel-6.5.12 if vendor confirms. I'll push for expedited change control.
Evelyn: customer comms draft ready: will send to ops@redwood with subject: "Incident: p95 latency spike (us-west-1) — mitigation in place". includes timeline, affected customers, current status, next steps.
Samir: final notes for in-incident RCA: keep timeline, include perf and eBPF artifacts links, attach kernel package names, and copy vendor ticket IDs. I'll start the timeline doc and paste in this thread.
Cheng: great work triaging quickly. I'll keep this thread open for handoff to postmortem. If anyone is leaving rotation, ping @Devon as shadow.
Devon: standing by to help with rollback validation and traffic cutover testing.
incident-bot: Incident closed by Cheng at 2392004820 — mitigation confirmed, p95 returned to normal for region us-west-1. Follow-up: create postmortem within 72h.
